scope.q: What is the typical output format and required data granularity for these grant reports, and for which external stakeholders are they primarily intended?
scope.why: Understanding the precise output specifications (e.g., PDF, Excel, specific tables) and target audience is critical to defining the reporting engine's requirements and validation criteria.

scope.q: Are the 'different reporting rules' mostly structured and quantitative (e.g., spending categories, deadlines) or do they involve significant qualitative interpretation and narrative generation?
scope.why: This determines the technical approach; highly structured rules can be codified directly, while subjective rules might require advanced NLP or human-in-the-loop workflows.

scope.q: What is the current volume of active grants, the average reporting frequency, and how often do new reporting rule sets or changes to existing ones typically occur?
scope.why: Quantifying the scale and volatility helps assess the necessary system robustness, scalability, and the effort required for ongoing rule maintenance.

decomposition.title: Current State Analysis & Knowledge Formalization
decomposition.why: This piece is about extracting and structuring the implicit knowledge currently held by the single person and the spreadsheet into an explicit, shareable format.

decomposition.title: Structured Rule Definition & Storage
decomposition.why: We need a robust way to define, store, and manage the diverse reporting rules so they can be programmatically applied, moving beyond a single person's understanding.

decomposition.title: Grant Data Ingestion & Harmonization
decomposition.why: The existing spreadsheet data needs to be systematically ingested, validated, and transformed into a normalized, queryable data model suitable for automated processing.

decomposition.title: Dynamic Report Generation Engine
decomposition.why: This is the core logic that applies the defined reporting rules to the harmonized grant data to produce compliant and accurate reports for various grants.

decomposition.title: Reporting Workflow & User Interface
decomposition.why: Users need an intuitive way to request reports, view status, and potentially manage rules, ensuring ease of use and reducing reliance on manual intervention.

decomposition.title: Output & Auditability Framework
decomposition.why: Ensuring the generated reports are accurate, verifiable, and delivered in the correct format is crucial for trust and compliance, requiring robust validation and logging.

sprint.title: Kickoff & Initial Rule/Data Schema Design
sprint.deliv: Documented schema for a generic grant data model and a draft structure for defining one specific type of reporting rule.

sprint.title: Spreadsheet Data Ingestion MVP
sprint.deliv: Python script or service that extracts data from the existing spreadsheet and loads it into a temporary structured database for one grant type.

sprint.title: Rule Management Service & Storage PoC
sprint.deliv: CRUD API endpoints for defining and retrieving a single, simple reporting rule, backed by a persistent database.

sprint.title: Core Report Generation Logic (Single Rule)
sprint.deliv: Service that can take a specific grant ID and a single rule ID, fetch data, apply the rule, and output a basic, structured report (e.g., JSON).

sprint.title: Basic UI for Report Request & Display
sprint.deliv: Web interface allowing a user to select a grant and rule, trigger report generation, and view the raw output from the core logic.

sprint.title: End-to-End Pilot with One Grant Type
sprint.deliv: Fully functional system capable of ingesting data for one specific grant, applying its primary reporting rule, and generating a validated report via the UI.

sprint.title: Validation, Feedback, & Planning
sprint.deliv: Detailed walk-through with the 'one person' to validate the pilot report, gather feedback, and outline the next set of rules to implement.

risks.risk: The 'one person's' undocumented knowledge about reporting rules is more complex or contradictory than anticipated, making formalization difficult.
risks.mitigation: Conduct intensive, structured interviews with the subject matter expert, recording edge cases and ambiguities, then prioritize explicit rule definition over implicit interpretation.

risks.risk: The existing spreadsheet data has significant quality issues (inconsistencies, missing values, unstructured fields) that hinder automated processing.
risks.mitigation: Implement a robust data validation and cleansing pipeline during ingestion, with clear error reporting and a feedback loop to the data source owner for correction.

risks.risk: New grant agreements introduce novel reporting requirements that don't fit the established rule definition framework, requiring frequent system re-engineering.
risks.mitigation: Design the rule definition framework with extensibility in mind (e.g., pluggable rule types, configurable parameters) and conduct regular reviews of new grant requirements to anticipate changes.

risks.risk: Stakeholders distrust automated reports due to a lack of transparency or an inability to audit how specific figures were derived.
risks.mitigation: Build in clear audit trails for each report, detailing which rules were applied and which data points were used, potentially allowing drill-down into source data and rule logic directly from the report.
